### About Fall Creek Farm & Nursery
**Fall Creek®** is a world-leading blueberry genetics company, founded in Oregon, United States, in 1978.
Today, the family-owned company delivers over 40 million plants of more than 100 varieties annually to leading growers and communities in over 65 countries through 10 wholly owned business units spanning North America, South America, Europe, Asia and Africa.
Fall Creek’s genetics and expertise power two distinct programs, each with its own path to success.
Sekoya® is a coordinated commercial platform, delivering a consistently outstanding consumer experience through a select network of licensees and growers.
Fall Creek® Collection offers premium, proven and distinctive genetics with the commercial flexibility for growers to build their own way forward.
Same breeding excellence.
Same technical foundation.
Two programs.
One shared commitment to better blueberries.
With more than 1,100 team members worldwide, Fall Creek provides comprehensive horticultural support and continues to lead industry innovation in blueberry genetics.
Our expansion into raspberries and blackberries marks the newest chapter.
...

# Fall Creek hosts first Global High Chill Field + Forum at Oregon Home Base, showcasing new blueberry genetics
Fall Creek Farm and Nursery, Inc.
will host its 2026 Global High Chill Field + Forum on July 29 at the company's research farm in Oregon, marking the first time the annual event has gone global.
The expanded format brings together growers, Sekoya program licensees and their growers, and select retailers from North America, Chile, and Northern Europe's high-chill growing regions, timed to peak ripening season at the site where the company generates its trial data.
The event will feature FC11-164, the company's first machine-harvestable blueberry variety for the fresh market, alongside Sekoya Nova FC15-173.
Growers have seen both varieties in the field at past events, but this year marks their first time being featured as official varieties, including the live reveal of FC11-164's official name.
With space limited and just three weeks remaining before the event, the firm is encouraging growers, licensees, and retail partners to register now to secure a place in the program.
...
## Fall Creek Collection FC11-164, a breakthrough in machine harvest
The company will give growers a look at FC11-164, the company's first machine-harvestable variety for the fresh market, developed to help growers manage rising labor costs in high-chill regions.
The variety will launch under the Fall Creek Collection program, with its official name announced live at the Field + Forum.
FC11-164 produces large fruit with a light blue color and firmness beyond any other variety the firm has evaluated, firm enough to be machine-harvested for the fresh market while holding excellent quality after 60 days or more in storage.
The variety ripens mid- to late-season and carries a mildly sweet flavor.
...
### A program built for a global audience
This year's expanded global format reflects the growing reach of Fall Creek's two genetics platforms, the Fall Creek Collection and the Sekoya licensing programs, and aligns with the event theme: “One Company.
Two Programs.
Endless Possibilities.”
Fall Creek CEO Marc de Beer will open the program with a keynote on Fall Creek's long-term investments in innovation, research, and grower-focused solutions supporting the future of the blueberry industry.
Sandefur will share insights on emerging areas of research and innovation influencing the future of blueberry production.
The afternoon program shifts to the commercial side, with sessions exploring consumer and retail insights shaping variety decisions across the supply chain.
A moderated panel featuring growers and marketers from the Fall Creek Collection and Sekoya programs will discuss evolving consumer and retailer expectations, followed by a session on new pathways for accessing Fall Creek genetics and a review of the blind tasting results.

# Fall Creek’s Paul Nselel: “Better berries can grow demand as well as replace older varieties”
Blueberry genetics and nursery company Fall Creek is expanding into raspberries and blackberries following its acquisition of Italy’s Berryplant and sister company Berrytech earlier this year.
Speaking at Fruit Attraction this month in Madrid, Chief Commercial Officer Paul Nselel explained the expansion, Fall Creek's new blueberry varieties, and whether better genetics can increase consumption while improving grower returns.
...
## What is the thinking behind the acquisition of Berryplant and Berrytech?
Fall Creek started as a blueberry nursery company and then evolved into breeding.
We have been fortunate to benefit from our customers’ trust, and a few years ago we began developing a diversification strategy.
After extensive work, we concluded that raspberries and blackberries were the adjacent crops that made sense.
Berrytech and Berryplant were a good fit because of their innovation, the trust they had built with customers, and their being a family company.
There was alignment around people, product quality, and service.
We had already started breeding raspberries on a small scale.
The acquisition is the next step.
...
### What does the acquisition bring to Fall Creek, and where can these varieties grow?
It starts with genetics, but plant quality is equally important.
Berrytech and Berryplant bring both breeding innovation and the ability to deliver exceptional plants.
In some locations, Fall Creek uses third-party nurseries, but the focus remains on genetics and plant quality.
Their genetics are grown in Morocco, Spain, Portugal, Italy, and Mexico, and to a lesser extent in Central America, including Guatemala.
...
### What is new in Fall Creek's blueberry portfolio?
We go to market through two platforms: Sekoya and the Fall Creek Collection.
Our varieties are doing very well.
Sekoya Pop is one of our flagship varieties, with millions of plants established around the world.
Over the past 12 months, we have released Sekoya Nova, a high-chill variety, and Everlast in the Fall Creek Collection.
Both demonstrate the innovation we are delivering to growers.
...
### Do royalties for improved genetics translate into better grower economics?
There are three drivers of grower economics: the yield in the field, the cost of labor, and the price they are getting at retail, which is closely correlated with quality.
Our breeding program focuses on all three.
We work to deliver higher yields and develop varieties that are harvestable by machine, reducing labor costs.
We also focus on characteristics consumers value: sweetness, size, and crunchiness.
...
### Do consumers recognize the improvement?
**Fall Creek gets exclusive rights for EasyRose ‘ALEL101’ raspberry**

# Fall Creek Connect Day highlights genetics, plant quality and regional growth opportunities
Fall Creek South Africa's Connect Day brought growers and industry stakeholders together for a programme focused on genetic innovation, nursery quality, applied research and the commercial requirements in the Southern African blueberry industry.
...
**Genetics as the foundation**
Jean Kotze, Applied Research Lead South Africa, shares about the long development cycle behind new blueberry genetics.
"The future success of this industry is dependent on today's genetic innovation."
With commercial varieties potentially requiring eight to 15 years of development, breeders must anticipate future production and market requirements well in advance.
He stresses that this requires information from growers, marketers and consumers.
Fall Creek's breeding programme operates across Oregon, Mexico and Spain, while applied research evaluates promising selections across multiple environments.
According to Jean, the programme currently involves approximately 300 crosses and 30,000 seedlings, with promising material progressing through increasingly extensive trial stages.
Applied research then evaluates genetics under commercial conditions through partnerships with growers.
"We rely on the observations of the grower as well as our own during this time."
This approach allows selections to be assessed against local climate, production systems and management practices.
He also highlights the potential of genetic markers to improve the efficiency of breeding for specific traits.
...
**From trials to practical evaluation**
The programme concluded with a nursery tour and test-block showcase, allowing attendees to examine production practices and evaluate selected genetics directly.
Varieties were presented for tasting and discussion, linking the technical presentations with practical observations in the field.
Across the day, a consistent theme emerged: genetic innovation, nursery quality, local testing, and grower support are interconnected components of commercial blueberry production.

# 10 years of blueberry innovation: how a watermelon field became a continental Hub
Fall Creek Farm & Nursery, Inc., a world-leading company in blueberry genetics and nursery production, is marking 10 years of operations in Spain this month.
What began in 2016 as a two-hectare harvest using plug material sourced from the United States has grown into the company's primary operational hub for Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA), now serving customers in 52 countries and producing 14 million plants per year.
The Fall Creek® nursery in Spain will celebrate its tenth anniversary on 28 May with an event at its Aznalcázar facilities, bringing together more than 250 employees, including over 30 people who have been part of the Fall Creek® family since the beginning in 2016.
...
**From a watermelon field to a continental hub**
Fall Creek® acquired its first farm in Spain in the summer of 2015: 16 hectares of agricultural land in Aznalcázar, Seville, a plot the founding team came to call "the watermelon field."
The nursery completed its first harvest in 2016 on just two hectares, using plug material from the company's nurseries in the United States.
From there, a decade of expansion and capability-building followed: propagation, tissue culture, applied research, and plant breeding facilities were progressively added across Aznalcázar and a purpose-built research farm in Villamanrique.
Today, Fall Creek® Spain operates a tissue culture laboratory, propagation facilities, a full applied research and development program, and the EMEA headquarters, the infrastructure of a company that came to Andalusia to stay.
...
Fall Creek® arrived in Spain at a time when European and North African growers had limited legal access to high-performance blueberry genetics and the clean, certified plant material needed to expand production with confidence.
The nursery in Spain changed that reality.
As the only facility in Spain capable of producing clean, uniform, true-to-type blueberry plants at scale for the EMEA region, Fall Creek® Spain gave growers access to world-class genetics on commercial terms that worked for them: legal, reliable, and at volume.
...
The nursery in Spain has served as the primary gateway for the Sekoya® and Fall Creek® Collection licensing platforms in European and North African markets, as well as acting as an early-adoption and validation centre for new genetics in the region.
The applied research programme at Villamanrique has been central to that work: Fall Creek® Collection Apex 'FCM14-057', which has generated exceptional demand since its commercial launch, was identified as a standout variety through applied research in Spain, demonstrating its potential under local conditions where it had gone unnoticed elsewhere.
The Spain team has also pioneered growing systems and plant production protocols that Fall Creek® has since adopted across its global operations.
...
**The road ahead**
As Fall Creek® enters its second decade in Spain, the Aznalcázar and Villamanrique facilities are positioned to shape the next chapter of the blueberry industry in EMEA, just as they have over the past ten years.
A new generation of varieties from the breeding programme in Spain, the result of nearly a decade of applied work in low-chill environments, is expected to reach the market in the coming seasons, offering growers in the region genetics developed specifically for European and North African growing conditions for the first time.

message.content:
# Investigative conclusion — evidence through **20 October 2026**

**No evidence located establishes that Fall Creek Farm & Nursery edits blueberry genomes or has commercialized a gene-edited blueberry.** Fall Creek’s documented blueberry pipeline is based on crossing and selection, global phenotypic trials, tissue-culture propagation, DNA fingerprinting and an emerging—not yet routine—use of marker-assisted/genomic selection. Its patents reviewed are **asexually reproduced plant-variety patents**, not CRISPR inventions. Independent scientific work has demonstrated CRISPR editing in blueberry, but largely as laboratory proof-of-concept; that work should not be attributed to Fall Creek. [149][194][345][347]

The confirmed berry-editing relationships are instead:

1. **Pairwise + PSI/PSG:** edited **caneberries**, especially blackberry; the compact blackberry reached limited consumer sales in Colombia, while seedless material remained in field testing. [243][254][330]  
2. **J.R. Simplot + PSI/PSG:** gene-edited **strawberry** development announced in 2021; no named commercial cultivar, regulator decision or sale was established by the cutoff. [75]  
3. **Plantik + Hudson River Biotechnology:** transgene-free genome editing for **heat-tolerant strawberry**, with validation underway but commercial field trials projected for 2028—therefore not commercial by the cutoff. [315][324]  
4. **Planasa:** conventional/technology-assisted berry breeding is documented, but gene editing by Planasa was **not established in this research pass**. [105]  
5. **Ohalo Boosted Breeding:** a separate proprietary breeding system. It may use gene editing to create breeding parents, but **“Boosted Breeding” is not a synonym for CRISPR**, and none of Fall Creek, Planasa, PSI/PSG, Simplot, Pairwise, Plantik or HRB appeared on Ohalo’s disclosed strawberry-consortium roster. [404][415]

---

## 1. Entities, legal identities, aliases, parents and subsidiaries

| Entity | Official domain / legal identity | Parents, subsidiaries and aliases | Finding relevant to berries and editing |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Fall Creek** | [fallcreeknursery.com](https://www.fallcreeknursery.com/); **Fall Creek Farm and Nursery, Inc.**, Oregon corporation; HQ/nursery: 39318 Jasper–Lowell Road, Lowell, Oregon. Federal records also render the name in capitals. [9][11][14] | Trade styles: **Fall Creek®**, Fall Creek Farm & Nursery, Fall Creek® Farm and Nursery. Privately held and family-owned. The company reported ten wholly owned business units by 2026, but a complete legal-entity list is not publicly presented. [5][188] | Blueberry genetics, plants and grower support. Documented breeding technologies do **not** establish genome editing. |
| **Fall Creek China** | Native Chinese identity: **云南富瑞科生物科技有限公司** (*Yunnan Furui Ke Biotechnology Co., Ltd.*), described as Fall Creek’s seventh wholly owned subsidiary. It operates a nursery and demonstration farm in Yunnan. [374][376] | A December 2025 Chinese registration reported separately is **上海臻可莓生物科技有限公司**, shareholder **Fall Creek Farm and Nursery The Netherlands B.V.**; this later entity’s precise operational relationship to 云南富瑞科 was not established from an original registry extract in this pass. [378] | Chinese nursery, demonstration and sale of selected blueberry genetics—not evidence of editing in China. |
| **Fall Creek Italy / Berryplant / Berrytech** | Fall Creek announced acquisition of Italian **Berryplant** and **Berrytech** on **10 June 2026**. Full registered suffixes were not given in the reviewed announcement. [210] | Berryplant’s nursery assets were to be integrated into **Fall Creek Italia**; Berrytech was initially to remain standalone. Berrytech, founded in 2019, held the Rubus breeding program and IP portfolio. Financial terms undisclosed. [211][214] | Adds raspberry and blackberry breeding/propagation. No editing technology was disclosed. |
| **Plant Sciences, Inc.** | Historically [plantsciences.com](https://www.plantsciences.com/); **Plant Sciences, Inc. (PSI)**, Watsonville, California, founded in 1985. [284] | In 2023 its breeding interests were reorganized into PSG. PSI remained a contracted research and propagation provider. [285] | Germplasm and commercial/nursery partner for Pairwise caneberries and Simplot strawberries. |
| **Plant Sciences Genetics** | [plantsciencesgenetics.com](https://www.plantsciencesgenetics.com/); **Plant Sciences Genetics, Inc. (PSG)**. [285] | Created from PSI and the breeding/IP interests of **Berry Genetics, Strawberry Sciences, Via Berry Breeding, Vitae Caneberry Breeding** and **Fragaria Plant Sciences**. PSG received 15 breeding populations: eight strawberry, three blueberry, two raspberry, one blackberry and one black raspberry. [285] | PSG says Pairwise editing covers caneberry programs and Simplot editing covers strawberry programs. That statement does **not** establish editing in PSG’s blueberry programs. [291] |
| **J.R. Simplot** | [simplot.com](https://www.simplot.com/); **J.R. Simplot Company**, privately held family company, Boise, Idaho. **Simplot Plant Sciences** is a division, not shown as a separate parent. [294][297] | No parent established; broad agrifood group. In 2018 Simplot licensed foundational CRISPR-Cas9 rights from Corteva and the Broad Institute. [82] | Supplies editing technology; PSI supplies strawberry germplasm and leads commercialization. |
| **Pairwise** | [pairwise.com](https://www.pairwise.com/); regulatory filings use **Pairwise Plants Services, Inc.** Other databases sometimes say Pairwise Plants LLC, but the legal relationship between those forms was not resolved here. [241][274] | Founded 2017 in Durham, North Carolina. No corporate parent established. Investors include Deerfield, Aliment Capital, Leaps by Bayer, Temasek and Corteva Catalyst. [269][273] | Confirmed CRISPR developer and owner/licensor of Fulcrum®. Caneberry partner is PSI/PSG—not Fall Creek. |
| **Hudson River Biotechnology** | [hudsonriver.bio](https://www.hudsonriver.bio/); **Hudson River Biotechnology B.V.**, Dutch Chamber of Commerce 63335611, Wageningen. Alias: **HRB**, sometimes shortened to Hudson River. [91][96] | Described by Pairwise as an **independent** Netherlands company; no parent established. [95] | BioMaas/protoplast-CRISPR, plant regeneration and trait-development service provider; licensed Pairwise Fulcrum in 2026. |
| **Plantik Biosciences** | [plantik.bio](https://www.plantik.bio/); **PLANTIK BIOSCIENCES**, French **SAS**, SIREN 853 088 441, registered 8 August 2019. [299][301] | No parent or subsidiaries established. Paris/Station F contact; registered-office and Genopole R&D addresses differ in secondary records. [303] | ATLANTIS target discovery and “dark-genome” regulatory-DNA editing. Strawberry partner is HRB. |
| **Planasa** | [planasa.com](https://planasa.com/); public sources identify **Plantas de Navarra, S.A.** and, in some corporate references, **TIGRUTI ITG S.L.** The exact current relationship between those legal entities was not established from an original registry extract. [104] | Acquired in 2023/24 by German family holding **EW Group**, which reports more than 300 subsidiaries. Planasa subsidiaries/operations include Planitalia and businesses in Mexico, China and other countries; it acquired Illinois Foundation Seeds in 2026. [359][363] | Breeds strawberry, blueberry, raspberry and blackberry using “traditional breeding methods and modern technology”; no Planasa CRISPR program was established. [105] |
| **Ohalo Genetics** | [ohalo.com](https://www.ohalo.com/); **Ohalo Genetics, Inc.** [418] | Formed in 2019 through The Production Board; no direct corporate link to the principal companies above was established. [414] | Included because of the “Boosted Breeding” ambiguity—not because it was shown to edit Fall Creek or Planasa berries. |

### Fall Creek operating geography versus headquarters

| Function | Established geography | Evidence and limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Corporate headquarters | Lowell, Oregon, USA | Corporate, accounting, legal, executive, propagation and production functions are described at Jasper–Lowell Road. [14] |
| Core breeding | **Oregon, Mexico and Spain** | Fall Creek stated that breeding operates across these three locations; about 300 crosses and 30,000 seedlings were reportedly active in October 2026. [169] |
| Applied research / validation | More than 140 grower and trial environments globally | Selections are evaluated under local climates and commercial systems; these sites are not necessarily Fall Creek-owned R&D facilities. [172][198] |
| Nursery/R&D footprint | USA, Mexico, Peru, Chile, Spain, Netherlands, South Africa and China | Corporate descriptions sometimes blur nurseries, R&D centres and commercial offices. Only Oregon/Mexico/Spain were specifically identified as the three breeding locations. [134][386] |
| China | Yunnan nursery and demonstration farm | Native name **云南富瑞科生物科技有限公司**. No Chinese blueberry-editing laboratory or edited product was established. [374] |
| EMEA hub | Andalusia, Spain | Spain became Fall Creek’s principal EMEA propagation/export hub, producing a reported 14 million finished plants annually and serving 52 countries. [184] |

---

## 2. Conventional, advanced and genome-editing technologies

| Company/program | Technology actually evidenced | Stage by 20 Oct 2026 | What must **not** be inferred |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Fall Creek blueberry breeding** | Controlled crossing/pollination, phenotypic selection, multi-location trials, high-throughput phenotyping, tissue-culture propagation, DNA fingerprinting for true-to-type identity; investment in genomics and DNA-informed breeding. [10][174][194] | Conventional breeding and field testing are routine and commercial. Marker-assisted and genomic selection were described in 2024 as proof-of-concept/future routine use. | DNA fingerprinting, tissue culture, genomics, “advanced genetics” and “breeding technology” do **not** prove gene editing. No Fall Creek CRISPR product, experiment, license or regulator submission was found. |
| **Scientific blueberry CRISPR—not Fall Creek** | *Agrobacterium*-mediated CRISPR/Cas9 editing of **CEN** and **PDS** in tetraploid highbush blueberry; one study obtained mutations in 6 of 47 transgenic lines, another reported low-to-moderate guide efficiencies. [345][347][354] | Laboratory proof-of-concept and functional genomics. A 2026 review said blueberry editing remained limited. [348] | These academic demonstrations are not evidence that Fall Creek, Planasa or PSG has an edited blueberry product. |
| **Pairwise Fulcrum®** | Integrated CRISPR tools, enzymes, multiplex editing and trait libraries. Pairwise patents cover altered fruit/seed development and MIXTA-family edits for thornless Rubus. [255][340][342] | Demonstrated in greenhouse and field material; compact blackberry sold on a limited basis in Colombia. Seedless version in field testing. | The existence of a “seedless, thornless, compact” stack does not mean every marketed Pairwise blackberry carries all three traits. |
| **PSI/PSG + Pairwise** | Pairwise edits PSI/PSG germplasm; PSG supplies base varieties, nursery/field expertise and propagation. Public-private Rubus diversity work also involved USDA-ARS, Arkansas, Cornell and NC State. [21][25] | Caneberry program demonstrated; compact edited blackberry commercial validation in Colombia. Red/black raspberry commercial products were not established. | PSG has blueberry breeding populations, but its Pairwise relationship is expressly described as **caneberry**, not blueberry. |
| **Simplot + PSI/PSG** | CRISPR-Cas9 and other new breeding techniques in proprietary strawberry germplasm; proposed traits include shelf life, waste reduction, yield and horticultural/pest/disease performance. Simplot edits; PSI/PSG grows and commercializes. [75] | Program announced; no named edited strawberry or documented sale by cutoff. | The companies’ 2021 expectation of launch “in the coming years” is not proof that launch occurred. |
| **HRB BioMaas / TiGER** | Transient/protoplast delivery of CRISPR components, regeneration from an edited single cell and screening of regeneration conditions; positioned as transgene-free editing directly in elite germplasm. [92][317] | Strawberry regeneration demonstrated; more than 30 strawberry genotypes reportedly tested. Product-level commercialization not established. [324] | “Transgene-free” describes the final plant/process claim; it does not mean “not genome edited.” |
| **HRB + Pairwise** | On **26 May 2026**, HRB licensed Fulcrum for integration into BioMaas services covering vegetables, soft fruit and other species. [95] | Technology/service license. No named product resulted from the announcement. | It is not evidence that Pairwise transferred its Fontana/seedless-blackberry product rights to HRB. |
| **Plantik ATLANTIS™** | Machine learning and multi-omics identify non-coding regulatory DNA targets; CRISPR then modifies regulatory switches rather than necessarily knocking out protein-coding genes. [66][321] | Heat-tolerant tomato proof-of-concept; strawberry-target validation underway with HRB. | “Dark genome” editing is still genome editing. Plantik’s tomato results do not prove a heat-tolerant strawberry already exists commercially. |
| **Plantik + HRB strawberry** | Plantik contributes heat-tolerance targets validated in tomato; HRB makes transgene-free edits in commercial strawberry germplasm. [315][320] | Validation underway; first commercial field trials were projected for spring/summer **2028**. [324] | No named breeder, cultivar, grower, regulator clearance or 2026 sale was established. |
| **Planasa** | Crossing, selection and field trials, supplemented by unspecified “modern technology”; traits include earliness, flavour, firmness, pathogen resistance, water efficiency and machine-harvest suitability. [105][106] | Commercial varieties and advanced selections. | “Modern technology,” “genetic improvement” and event participation with Fall Creek are not evidence of CRISPR. |
| **Ohalo Boosted Breeding™** | Ohalo says novel proteins/techniques suppress reproductive circuits so each parent transmits its complete genome, generating polyploid progeny and uniform hybrid/true seed. Its potato patents contemplate inducing clonal gametes and may route selected lines through editing or modification. [415][418] | Strawberry consortium and field-development programs; no commercially available Boosted strawberry established. [419] | Do not replace “Boosted Breeding” with “CRISPR” in descriptions. CRISPR may be an enabling tool, while Boosted Breeding denotes the reproductive/breeding system and resulting inheritance pattern. |
